validated_results.title: Selenium and risk of bladder cancer: a population-based case-control study.
validated_results.reason: This population-based case-control study evaluated the association between toenail selenium levels and incident bladder cancer risk.

sample_size.excerpt: We interviewed a total of 857 bladder cancer cases and 1,191 controls (85% of cases, 70% of controls participated) and obtained toenail selenium levels for 1,875 of the 2,048 (92%) eligible subjects, including 767 of the 857 (89.5%) cases and 1,108 of the 1,191 (93%) controls.

cases.excerpt: We interviewed a total of 857 bladder cancer cases and 1,191 controls (85% of cases, 70% of controls participated) and obtained toenail selenium levels for 1,875 of the 2,048 (92%) eligible subjects, including 767 of the 857 (89.5%) cases and 1,108 of the 1,191 (93%) controls.

effect_size.excerpt: Overall, toenail selenium concentrations were not significantly related to bladder cancer [OR Q4 versus Q1, 0.90 (95% CI, 0.68−1.19); P trend = 0.15].

confidence_interval.excerpt: Overall, toenail selenium concentrations were not significantly related to bladder cancer [OR Q4 versus Q1, 0.90 (95% CI, 0.68−1.19); P trend = 0.15].

p_value.excerpt: Overall, toenail selenium concentrations were not significantly related to bladder cancer [OR Q4 versus Q1, 0.90 (95% CI, 0.68−1.19); P trend = 0.15].

design.excerpt: We investigated the association between toenail selenium concentrations and bladder cancer risk in a population-based case-control study in New Hampshire.

timing.excerpt: We analyzed data from 857 incidence cases diagnosed between July 1, 1994 and June 30, 2001 and 1,191 general population controls.

continent.excerpt: We investigated the association of toenail selenium concentration with bladder cancer incidence in a large population-based case-control study from New Hampshire.

ethnicity.excerpt: To be eligible for the study, we required that subjects have a listed telephone number and speak English.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Additionally, subjects were asked to provide toenail samples, which were analyzed for selenium using an established protocol and an instrumental neutron activation analysis at the University of Missouri Research Reactor Center

smoking_status.excerpt: In each regression analysis, we controlled for age (linear), sex, and pack-years of smoking.

additional_extractions.comparison_type: Highest versus lowest quartile of toenail selenium, women

effect_size.excerpt: However, within specific subgroups there were inverse associations, i.e., among moderate smokers [OR, 0.61 (95% CI, 0.39-0.96); P(trend) = 0.004], women [OR, 0.66 (95% CI, 0.40-1.10); P(trend) = 0.11], and those with p53-positive cancers [OR Q4 versus Q1, 0.57 (95% CI, 0.34-0.94); P(trend) = 0.01]. Our results indicate that selenium is not inversely related to risk of bladder cancer overall; however, they raise the possibility that selenium may be preventive in certain molecular phenotypes of tumors (e.g., p53 positive) or within certain subsets of a population (e.g., women or moderate smokers).
